title: Protected RBAC and authorization administration
summary: Introduced protected role-based authorization, context-aware sessions, exact directory synchronization, suspension controls, and complete Admin authorization management.
changes: Introduced four protected roles and thirteen code-owned permissions enforced through application-owned Gate and policy decisions, with provenance-guarded direct user permissions available only to central authorization services.

Added source-provenanced role assignments with mandatory persisted actors for local grants and actor-free non-local sources, authorization epochs, context-aware password, Cloudron OIDC, and local quality-assurance sessions, plus suspension and forced reauthentication controls.
Added exact normalized directory-group mappings, catalogue synchronization, eligibility revocation, and lifecycle commands for guarded activation and verification.
Added accessible Admin Users, Groups, Roles, and Permissions sections with transactional assignment, mapping, suspension, custom-role, and final-super-admin safeguards.
Aligned Admin user permission inventories with the runtime Gate by combining role and provenanced direct grants without exposing an arbitrary direct-assignment interface.
Restricted assignment and operational notifications to unsuspended staff whose protected baseline and qualifying provenance agree, with uniform authorization-first denial handling.

Bound and coalesced directory synchronization work, made final and repeated queue-failure callbacks durably invalidate prior directory sessions while clearing only their matching lease, and pinned the production application environment.

Serialized privileged mutations behind authorization-state locks with session, epoch, generation, exact-role provenance, and present-group revalidation, including one final-super-admin predicate shared by runtime and lifecycle checks.
Derived deployment-control trust directly from the exact Git revision before third-party actions or dependencies and published root-owned, application-non-writable activation and rollback controls.
affected_areas: Authentication sessions, authorization, policies, and account suspension
Directory group catalogue, mappings, synchronization, and revocation
Admin Users, Groups, Roles, and Permissions
Authorization migration, activation, verification, and rollback compatibility
version_rationale: A backward-compatible minor release completing the protected authorization and administration capability planned in issue #10.
validation: Automated tests cover the guarded cutover, exact source and pivot parity, roleless and interrupted retries, protected permission matrix, actor-attributed local grants, actor-free non-local sources, direct-permission inventory parity, correlated provenance, session context, suspension, assignment integrity, uniform denial responses, bounded directory synchronization, lifecycle commands, and Admin authorization boundaries.

The release gate requires complete SQLite coverage plus deterministic two-process row-lock and reconciliation tests and a real correlated queue-timeout probe on MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 11.4, queue and LDAP bounds, transaction-time privileged reauthorization, Git-derived deployment-control authentication, root-owned control-use checks, exact environment and rollback contracts, frontend tests, production assets, archive checks, and exact post-restart health and OIDC verification.
known_limitations: Issue #11 public identity and consent work is not included.
Issue #19 version-management automation is not included.
rollback: Code rollback is idempotent and bound to the exact failed and pre-activation releases, with complete runtime controls derived from the exact Git revision and consumed from a root-owned application-non-writable directory, while retaining the Phase B database migrations. A deliberate maintenance downgrade refuses unrepresentable revocation state and invalidates sessions first; the pre-deployment backup remains the database recovery boundary.
provenance: Defined by Phase B of MyAPES Account issue #10.

title: Guest authentication redirect correction
summary: Corrected protected-route handling so signed-out visitors reach Public Login instead of a server error.
changes: Directed browser guests from protected pages to the existing Public Login route while preserving their intended destination.
Restored unauthorized JSON responses for clients that explicitly request JSON.
affected_areas: Guest authentication redirects and protected-route error handling
version_rationale: A backward-compatible patch correcting guest access to the existing authentication entry point.
validation: Automated feature tests cover browser redirects, intended destinations, and unauthorized JSON responses.
The complete application, release-validation, frontend, build, cache, migration, and deployment checks remain required before release.
known_limitations: This correction does not change authentication methods, account authorization, or staff OIDC behavior.
rollback: Restore the previous application release, accepting that signed-out protected-route requests will again return a server error.
provenance: Defined by MyAPES Account issue #25 after the defect was reproduced during production acceptance.

title: Access-control compatibility foundation
summary: Added the transitional identity and access-level foundation required for the protected role-based access-control rollout while preserving current access behavior.
changes: Added explicit local and Cloudron identity classifications plus a centralized legacy access-level contract.
Kept the existing role field synchronized through application dual-writes and a transitional database guard so in-flight legacy writes remain compatible during cutover and rollback.
Added guarded pre-activation reconciliation with database-guard and postcondition checks for safe migration, rollback, and retry behavior.
affected_areas: User identity and access-level compatibility data
Authentication, directory revalidation, and staff-scoped application queries
Release activation and database compatibility checks
version_rationale: A backward-compatible minor release introducing the first independently deployable capability for the staged authorization architecture.
validation: Automated SQLite and MySQL upgrade, fresh-install, database-guard, dual-write, role-absent, authentication, authorization, and activation-order tests cover the compatibility contract.
The complete application test and build checks continue to verify unchanged public, staff, and administrator behavior.
known_limitations: This release does not add granular permissions, role-management pages, directory-group mappings, or the final role-based access-control system.
The legacy access level remains the authorization source until Phase B is separately deployed and verified.
Phase B must remove the transitional database guard before removing the legacy role column.
rollback: Restore the previous application release; the existing role field remains available and the transitional database guard keeps legacy writes aligned with the additive compatibility fields.
provenance: Defined by Phase A of MyAPES Account issue #10 as the compatibility release required before the protected RBAC rollout.

title: Post-merge release validation correction
summary: Corrected the bootstrap validation test so the release foundation remains verifiable after it is merged to the main branch.
changes: Changed the bootstrap comparison test to use the repository root commit, which permanently predates source-controlled release metadata.
Removed the incorrect assumption that origin/main remains a pre-release-contract base after the foundation is merged.
affected_areas: Release-history command regression coverage
Post-merge continuous integration and deployment gating
version_rationale: A compatible patch correcting a post-merge test assumption without changing the public Change Log Hub or release contract.
validation: The focused bootstrap comparison test and complete application suite pass when run from a branch based on the merged release foundation.
Append-only comparison against the current main branch confirms exactly one higher release record.
known_limitations: This patch changes test setup only and does not add a user-facing application capability.
rollback: Restore the earlier test base only if the release foundation is also removed from the main branch.
provenance: Defined during post-merge deployment verification for MyAPES Account issue #20.

title: Public Change Log Hub and semantic versioning
summary: Introduced a public, searchable MyAPES release history and a source-controlled semantic version contract for future releases.
changes: Added the public Change Log Hub with search, release filters, expandable records, current-release navigation, and accessible result feedback.
Added a shared footer version link so guests, public users, and staff can reach the current release record from every application screen.
Added append-only release validation for pull requests and main-branch updates without creating a database-backed editor.
Separated the semantic application version from the immutable deployment commit identity in health and release verification.
affected_areas: Public Change Log Hub and shared application footer
Release metadata validation and continuous integration
Health reporting and immutable release packaging
version_rationale: A backward-compatible minor release establishing a new public capability and the release-management contract for later roadmap work.
validation: Release schema, append-only history, public access, footer consistency, health reporting, filtering behavior, and packaging contracts are covered by automated tests.
Responsive light and dark layouts, keyboard operation, focus visibility, reduced motion, and no-JavaScript readability are included in local acceptance.
known_limitations: Release history is reviewed source-controlled data and has no database editor.
No Git tag, GitHub Release, production deployment, or authenticated production acceptance is included in this release implementation pass.
rollback: Restore the previous application release; its deployment identity remains available through the existing immutable commit and code-rollback process.
provenance: Defined by MyAPES Account issue #20 and implemented as the release foundation for roadmap issue #17.
